key_terms.لُمَزَةٍ: Back-biter (one who points out people's faults)
key_terms.هُمَزَةٍ: Slanderer (one who stabs at people's backs with words)
key_terms.وَيْلٌ: Woe or destruction (a call for ruin)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Kull Humazah Lumazah' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the specific context of Abu Lahab or the general archetype of the hypocrite who uses verbal attacks to diminish the status of the righteous. The term 'humazah' (traduer) implies a subtle, insidious form of slander, while 'lumazah' (backbiter) suggests a more direct, repetitive mockery, highlighting the dual nature of this ethical vice. This serves as a foundational warning for the faithful to guard their tongues against the subtle corruption of reputation.
